source.title: LightNorm: Area and Energy-Efficient Batch Normalization Hardware for On-Device DNN Training
source.authors: Seock-Hwan Noh; Junsang Park; Dahoon Park; J. Koo; Jeik Choi; Jaeha Kung

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training results showing that reduced precision in BN can sharply lower accuracy in some settings, while range normalization and selected FP10 formats can preserve accuracy. This refines the scope of training stability claims; it does not test whether networks reach near-zero training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper studies BN approximations and hardware efficiency. Its training results report test accuracy and feature statistics, not training classification error or convergence to zero training error. No rows bear on V1–V6 as phrased; cited work on BN and optimization is prior work, not this paper's evidence.
record.test_reason: The study uses batch normalization and evaluates approximations to it and their hardware performance. It does not compare adding BN against no BN for accuracy gain or learning-rate tolerance, and its results do not test V1–V5. The record's tests/T5 classification is therefore incorrect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: combining low precision, range normalization and block floating point reduces hardware cost while approximately preserving accuracy in the selected configurations. Their accuracy-preservation claim allows model-specific losses: Table IV shows a 2.03-percentage-point decrease for ResNet-50 with group size four, despite an average decrease of about 0.5 points.
record.recipe_differences: Uses approximate BN computation and hardware evaluation; it does not test the original claim's optimization outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies substantially with BN precision and block floating point group size; FP8 for the forward pass degrades accuracy, and groups of 8 or 16 degrade accuracy sharply.

fits_no_version.finding: BN precision and range-normalization formats affect CNN accuracy. Table III reports MobileNetV1/V2 test accuracies of 67.82%/65.73% with FP10-A forward and FP10-B backward range normalization, versus 66.21%/65.38% with FP32 BN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected low-precision range-normalization formats can preserve CNN test accuracy relative to FP32 BN.

fits_no_version.finding: Table IV reports test accuracies with exponent-sharing groups of four within 2.03 percentage points of FP32 across four CNNs. Groups of sixteen reduce accuracy substantially in every model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Accuracy preservation with LightNorm depends on exponent-sharing group size and model.

fits_no_version.finding: The hardware evaluation estimates 1.3–5.0 times lower energy consumption per training epoch for the proposed accelerator than the compared configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LightNorm reduces the hardware cost of normalization and training in the evaluated accelerator configurations.

record.problems: The paper reports test accuracy rather than training error. Some results are plotted without exact values in text; the evidence addresses BN approximation accuracy and hardware costs, not the catalog claim's optimization outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: reported training experiments measure test accuracy and intermediate feature statistics, not training classification error or another measure of the versions' named behavior.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe effects.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Whether adding BN accelerates accuracy gains or permits higher learning rates; training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The paper sometimes calls its accuracy results training accuracy, while Tables III–IV explicitly report test accuracy. Neither those results nor Figure 5 provides the comparisons needed for V6. Hardware runtime savings do not establish faster optimization from adding BN. The empty row set is appropriate; the excluded findings are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and spurious minima.
Depth and residual shortcuts as determinants of training error.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth.
Learning rates above stability thresholds, curvature, and loss trajectories.
Whether adding BN speeds accuracy gain or tolerates higher learning rates; Fixup comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
